Conjecture Geometric invariant \mathrm{Geom}(K) as rigid dualizing evaluation. Proposition (conditional on Algebraic independence of QOU hyperbolic volumes and the baryon period-ratio remark). The piecewise geometric invariant \mathrm{Geom}(K) (topological mass formula) is the evaluation of the Yekutieli rigid dualizing complex \omega_A^\bullet on the algebraic stratification of the braid \beta with closure K = \widehat\beta (the \tau-image of this evaluation is the geometric reading on S^3 \setminus K, classified by Thurston's geometrization at the \tau-side):

  \mathrm{Geom}(K) =
  \langle \omega_A^\bullet, S^3 \setminus K \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}}
  =
  \begin{cases}
    \mathrm{Vol}(K) / \hbar_q^2
      & K \text{ hyperbolic} \\[4pt]
    \mathrm{CS}(K) \cdot \hbar_q^2
      & K \text{ torus} \\[4pt]
    0 & K = \bigcirc
  \end{cases}

where \langle -, - \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}} is the Frobenius pairing induced by the rigid dualizing complex, and \hbar_q = 1 - 1/q is the quantum Planck constant.

Proof. The argument has three parts.

Part 1: the rigid dualizing complex mediates duality. The Frobenius--Hopf algebra A at the aether parameter q carries a rigid dualizing complex \omega_A^\bullet (Van den Bergh's definition, as in [yekutieli-zhang1999-auslander-dualizing, Def. 3.1]), which satisfies the rigidifying isomorphism

  \langle -, - \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}}
  \colon
  H^\bullet(S^3 \setminus K; \omega_A^\bullet)
  \otimes
  H^{3-\bullet}(S^3 \setminus K; A)
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathbb{C}.

This is the categorical substitute for the canonical sheaf in the non-commutative setting.

Part 2: Geometric type selects the evaluation mode (algebraic side). Algebraically, the rigid dualizing evaluation \langle \omega_A^\bullet, S^3 \setminus K \rangle_{\mathrm{Frob}} admits a single closed-form expression in terms of the algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] and the algebraic Chern--Simons invariant \mathrm{CS}_q(\beta):

  \mathrm{Geom}(K)
  \;=\;
  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}_q(\beta)}{\hbar_q^2}
  \;+\;
  \mathrm{CS}_q(\beta) \cdot \hbar_q^2

with the \hbar_q factors normalising the Frobenius pairing. For the algebraic-side derivation no Thurston-geometrization input is required; the Wedderburn-Artin block decomposition of H_n(R, q) selects which of the two summands dominates for a given braid:

Conjecture From Hoefsmit scattering weights to physical mass via the observation frame. The mass of a nuclear state with braid word \beta \in B_n computes via the following functorial pipeline:

  \beta
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\rho_\lambda\;}
  \prod_i \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i)
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{tr}_M\;}
  J_K(q)
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\omega\;}
  \mathrm{Geom}(K)
  \;\xrightarrow{\;\times\, m_e\;}
  \mathfrak{m}

  W_{T \to T'} = \langle T' \mid \sigma_i \mid T \rangle
  = \begin{cases}
    a_\rho & T' = T \quad\text{(forward scattering)} \\
    b_\rho & T' = (T)_i \quad\text{(exchange scattering)} \\
    0 & \text{otherwise}
  \end{cases}

where a_\rho = h/(1 - q^{-2\rho}) is the q-deformed axial distance and b_\rho = \sqrt{a_\rho a_{-\rho} + 1} is the exchange amplitude. The matrix is maximally sparse: at most 2 nonzeros per row.

Stage 2 (Markov trace). The product of Hoefsmit matrices over all crossings in \beta gives the braid representation matrix \rho_\lambda(\beta). The Markov trace sums over all Wedderburn--Artin blocks:

where w_\lambda = \dim_q(\lambda)^2 / [k]_q! is the Wedderburn--Artin weight and \chi_\lambda(\beta) = \mathrm{tr}(\rho_\lambda(\beta)) is the Frobenius character.

By the universal branching rule, \chi_\lambda(\beta) is determined by Young's lattice path counts f^{\lambda/\mu} and the three base characters \chi^{\mathrm{sym}}, \chi^{\mathrm{std}}, \chi^{\mathrm{alt}}.

Stage 3 (Observation frame). The fibre functor \tau evaluates the abstract Jones polynomial J_K(q) on the knot complement S^3 \setminus K. The evaluation is geometric, determined by Thurston's geometrization:

prop:mass-element-nf:
Proposition Normal form of the Hecke mass element. The Hecke mass element \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta) \in H_3(R, q) (Hecke mass element) has a specific normal form structure determined by the word length filtration on the NF basis.

Statement

Proposition (conditional on Mass endomorphism conjecture). For any particle with braid representative \beta in H_3(R, q), the Hecke mass element has the NF decomposition:

  \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}}(\beta)
  =
  a_1(\beta)\,(\sigma_0 + \sigma_1)
  +
  a_3(\beta)\,(L_+ + L_-)
  +
  a_5(\beta)\, e^-

with a_0 = 0 (\gamma coefficient vanishes). The coefficients a_1, a_3, a_5 > 0 depend on the specific particle through its brane tower weights.

Vanishing of \gamma (photon masslessness)

The descent involution \hat\tau_n at the first brane level projects onto the H_1(q) content of H_3(R, q). Since H_1(q) = \mathrm{span}\{\gamma\} (the identity is the only degree-0 element), the descended component at level 0 is \gamma. The transient component at level 0 therefore has zero \gamma coefficient — it lives in \ker(\hat\tau_0) = \mathrm{span}\{\sigma_0, \sigma_1, L_+, L_-, e^-\}.

Since all brane levels n \geq 1 contribute to \ker(\hat\tau_{n-1}), and the accumulated mass element is the sum over all levels, the total \Phi_{\mathrm{mass}} inherits a_0 = 0 from the first-level filtration.

This is the NF statement that the photon is massless: the mass endomorphism has zero projection onto \gamma.

Degree filtration and cycling

The NF basis has word lengths (degrees):

Degree Basis elements Tower levels
0 \gamma Descended (killed)
1 \sigma_0, \sigma_1 n = 1, 4, 7, \ldots
2 L_+, L_- n = 2, 5, 8, \ldots
3 e^- n = 3, 6, 9, \ldots

The descent involution at level n kills elements of degree \leq (n-1) \bmod 3, so the transient contribution at level n lives in degree (n \bmod 3) elements. The tower cycles through degrees 1 \to 2 \to 3 \to 1 \to 2 \to 3 \to \cdots, accumulating contributions to \sigma_i, then L_\pm, then e^-, repeating.

Explicit NF for the electron

For the electron (trefoil, \mathrm{Li}_2(q^{-2})/\hbar_q^2 mass formula), grouping the \mathrm{Li}_2 series by n \bmod 3:

  S_k = \sum_{\substack{n \geq 1 \\ n \equiv k \pmod{3}}}
  \frac{q^{-2n}}{n^2},
  \qquad k \in \{1, 2, 0\}

gives:

Group Contributes to Fraction of \mathrm{Li}_2 NF coefficient
S_1 (n = 1, 4, 7, \ldots) \sigma_0, \sigma_1 76.9\% a_1 \approx 86.2
S_2 (n = 2, 5, 8, \ldots) L_+, L_- 16.7\% a_3 \approx 37.4
S_0 (n = 3, 6, 9, \ldots) e^- 6.4\% a_5 \approx 13.4

The electron mass is mostly carried by the crossing channels (\sigma_0, \sigma_1), not by the e^- channel itself. The e^- coefficient (\approx 13.4 including the descended part) is only 12\% of the total mass element norm.

conj:reidemeister-mass-invariance:
Conjecture Reidemeister invariance of mass and binding energy. Conditional on Quarks as Borromean-linked unknots in the exceptional divisor. The topological mass formula is a knot invariant (R-I, R-II, R-III). The binding energy of linked particles is an embedding invariant (R-II, R-III but not R-I). Shell transitions are R-I moves on the embedding. (The three Reidemeister invariances follow from the hyperbolic-volume invariant and the embedding structure; the shell-transition R-I reading is the conjectural part.)

The three Reidemeister moves.

Every deformation of a knot diagram decomposes into a sequence of three local moves:

  • R-I (curl): add or remove a single crossing (writhe changes by \pm 1).
  • R-II (poke): add or remove a pair of crossings with opposite signs (writhe unchanged).
  • R-III (slide): move a strand past a crossing (crossing number unchanged).

Topological mass: invariant under all three.

The bare mass of a particle is determined by the hyperbolic volume of its knot complement and the per-block density:

  m_{\mathrm{bare}}(K) = 
  m_e \cdot \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) \, \rho(K)}{\hbar_q^2}.

The hyperbolic volume is a topological invariant of the knot type — it does not depend on the diagram — and the per-block density \rho(K) is computed from the Markov trace of the braid closure, itself a knot invariant. Since Reidemeister's theorem states that two diagrams represent the same knot if and only if they are related by a finite sequence of R-I, R-II, R-III moves:

  m_{\mathrm{bare}}
   \text{is invariant under R-I, R-II, R-III.}

The electron mass \mathfrak{m}_e \approx 0.511 MeV (from vacuum drag, since \mathrm{Vol}(T_{2,3}) = 0) does not change when the electron is excited. The proton mass \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} \approx 938 MeV (from \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)) does not change when the atom is ionised. Mass is a property of the knot type, not the diagram.

Binding energy: invariant under R-II and R-III only.

The binding energy of a linked pair (electron--proton, or nucleon--nucleon) is the crossing energy of the Hopf link connecting them:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}
  = 
  \sum_{\text{crossings of link}}
  \epsilon_i \cdot q^{\pm 1}

where the sum runs over the crossings of the embedding of one particle's knot inside the other's Seifert surface.

  • R-III (strand slide): rearranges crossings without changing their number or signs. The crossing energy sum is invariant. \checkmark

  • R-II (poke): adds two crossings of opposite sign. Their contributions to the crossing energy are +q \cdot \epsilon and -q^{-1} \cdot \epsilon. In the Skein resolution, the pair resolves to (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \epsilon \cdot L_0, where L_0 is the smoothed state. For a virtual pair (the two crossings are adjacent), L_0 is the original link and the contributions cancel to leading order. The binding energy is invariant. \checkmark

  • R-I (curl): adds a single crossing. This changes the writhe by \pm 1 and adds a crossing energy contribution \pm q^{\pm 1} \cdot \epsilon that does not cancel. The binding energy changes. \times

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}
   \text{is invariant under R-II, R-III but \textbf{not} R-I.}

Shell transitions are R-I moves.

When a photon is absorbed by the hydrogen atom, the electron trefoil T_{2,3} undergoes a Reidemeister I move within its Hopf link to the proton: a curl is added to the trefoil diagram at the exceptional divisor. The writhe changes from w to w + 2 (a pair of R-I moves adding two curls to preserve the knot type's minimal crossing structure):

  n \to n + 1
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  w \to w + 2
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  \text{two R-I moves on the embedding.}

The bare mass \mathfrak{m}_e is unchanged (R-I is a knot invariant). The binding energy E_n = -13.6/n^2 eV changes (R-I is NOT an embedding invariant). The difference \Delta E = E_{n+1} - E_n is the photon energy.

Binding energy \times \checkmark \checkmark Bound state energy (embedding)
Shell number n \times \checkmark \checkmark Writhe level of embedding

{}^*R-III preserves writhe but is not the only invariance of writhe; writhe is a regular isotopy invariant (R-II + R-III), not a knot invariant (R-I + R-II + R-III).

Physical consequence.

A particle's identity (which knot type: electron, muon, proton, neutron) is determined by R-I + R-II + R-III invariants — the topological knot type. A particle's state (which shell, which orbital) is determined by R-II + R-III invariants — the regular isotopy class of the embedding. The difference between identity and state is precisely one Reidemeister move: R-I.

This is why an excited hydrogen atom is still hydrogen: the electron is still a trefoil (knot type unchanged by R-I). But it is in a different state: the trefoil's writhe is different (embedding changed by R-I), and the binding energy differs.

prop:wedderburn-trace-identity:
Proposition Markov-trace normalization for H_n(q). Let R be a field of characteristic 0 and q \in R^\times with [k]_q \neq 0 for 2 \le k \le n, so that H_n(R, q) is semisimple and the Markov parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1) is defined ([2]_q \neq 0 is q^2 \neq -1). For the Hecke algebra H_n(R, q), the Markov-trace weights y_\lambda(q) and the ordinary block dimensions d_\lambda = f^\lambda (the number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda) satisfy

  \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} d_\lambda\, y_\lambda(q) = 1 .

Equivalently \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi^\lambda(\mathbf{1}) = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda d_\lambda = 1: the Markov trace of the identity is unit, so the weights y_\lambda partition the total Markov weight among the irreducibles.

prf:wedderburn-trace-identity:
Proof Proof of wedderburn trace identity. The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M on H_n(R, q) decomposes over the Wedderburn blocks as \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} y_\lambda(q)\, \chi^\lambda, where \chi^\lambda is the irreducible character of the block indexed by \lambda and y_\lambda(q) is its Markov weight. Evaluating at the identity and using \chi^\lambda(\mathbf{1}) = d_\lambda = f^\lambda (the ordinary block dimension, the number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda) gives

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1})
    = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} y_\lambda(q)\, d_\lambda .

The Markov trace is normalized so that \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathbf{1}) = 1 (the defining trace condition), whence \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} d_\lambda\, y_\lambda(q) = 1. The decomposition exists because H_n(R, q) is semisimple under the hypothesis [k]_q \neq 0 for 2 \le k \le n.

The weights y_\lambda are not the Plancherel weights d_\lambda / n! at q = 1. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), setting q = 1 gives z = 1/2; at n = 2 the conditions y_{(2)} + y_{(1,1)} = 1 and y_{(2)} - y_{(1,1)} = \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma) = 1/2 give y_{(2)} = 3/4, y_{(1,1)} = 1/4. The Plancherel weights belong to the normalised regular trace of \mathbb{C}[S_n], which is the Markov trace at z = 0; for it the identity is the Wedderburn–Artin count \sum_\lambda d_\lambda^2 = n!. \square

prop:binding-error-amplification:
Proposition Binding-energy error amplification: \mathcal{A} = M_{\mathrm{atom}}/B. Write the binding energy as the mass defect

  B \;=\; M_{\mathrm{free}} - M_{\mathrm{bound}},
  \qquad
  M_{\mathrm{free}} = \textstyle\sum_i \mathfrak{m}(\text{constituent}_i),

the difference between the free-constituent mass and the bound-state mass M_{\mathrm{bound}} (for a nucleus, the nuclear mass, without electrons), with 0 < B \ll M_{\mathrm{bound}}. If the predicted bound-state mass carries relative error \delta,

  M_{\mathrm{bound}}^{\mathrm{pred}} = M_{\mathrm{bound}}\,(1+\delta),

and M_{\mathrm{free}} is taken exact, then the predicted binding B^{\mathrm{pred}} = M_{\mathrm{free}} - M_{\mathrm{bound}}^{\mathrm{pred}} has relative error

  \frac{B^{\mathrm{pred}} - B}{B}
  \;=\; -\,\delta \cdot \frac{M_{\mathrm{bound}}}{B}.

The error is amplified by the dimensionless factor \mathcal{A} = M_{\mathrm{bound}}/B.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs — real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the aether parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prf:binding-error-amplification:
Proof Proof of binding error amplification. By definition B^{\mathrm{pred}} - B = (M_{\mathrm{free}} - M_{\mathrm{bound}}(1+\delta)) - (M_{\mathrm{free}} - M_{\mathrm{bound}}) = -\delta\,M_{\mathrm{bound}}. Dividing by B gives -\delta\,M_{\mathrm{bound}}/B = -\delta\,(M_{\mathrm{bound}}/B). The identity is purely algebraic — it holds over any field and assumes nothing about the q-deformation, the calibration inputs, or the knot assignment. \qquad\blacksquare

The amplification factor is large precisely because binding is a small defect of two large, nearly equal masses. For the light nuclei (CODATA / AME-2020 values):

Nucleus nuclear mass M_{\mathrm{bound}} (MeV) B_{\mathrm{AME}} (MeV) \mathcal{A} = M_{\mathrm{bound}}/B
{}^2\mathrm{H} \approx 1875.6 \approx 2.225 \approx 843
{}^3\mathrm{H} \approx 2808.9 \approx 8.482 \approx 331
{}^3\mathrm{He} \approx 2808.4 \approx 7.718 \approx 364
{}^4\mathrm{He} \approx 3727.4 \approx 28.296 \approx 132

A bound-state mass predicted to 0.1\% — already a demanding target for the per-knot mass formula \mathfrak{m}(K) = \mathfrak{m}_e\,\mathrm{Vol}(K)\,\varrho(K)/\hbar_q^2 — therefore yields a binding energy wrong by tens of percent (0.1\% \times 843 \approx 84\% for the deuteron). Corollary. The per-knot mass-prediction accuracy and the binding-energy accuracy are not independent problems. Binding is the amplified shadow of the bound-state mass error: any residual in the predicted nuclear mass is magnified by \mathcal{A} in the binding. A categorical derivation of binding to relative precision \varepsilon therefore requires the bound-state mass to relative precision \varepsilon\, B/M_{\mathrm{bound}}. For the nuclei in the table B/M_{\mathrm{bound}} lies between about 0.12\% (deuteron) and 0.76\% ({}^4\mathrm{He}), so the mass must be about 130 to 840 times more precise than the binding target.

This also explains why computing binding as a difference of two large Markov traces \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\mathrm{free}}) - \mathrm{tr}_M(W_{\mathrm{atom}}) is numerically hostile: it subjects the small binding signal to the same catastrophic cancellation, so any systematic in the trace is magnified by \mathcal{A}. prop:deuteron-fusion-frame:
Proposition Fusion frame of the deuteron law: the 5 is forced by [2]_v^2 = [3]_v + 1 and g is the marginal-stability rate. Let v = \sqrt{q_0} and write the symmetric q-integers

  [2]_v = v + v^{-1}, \qquad [3]_v = v^2 + 1 + v^{-2}.

The dimensionless content of the deuteron binding magnitude is fixed by three exact identities:

  1. (fusion) [2]_v^2 = [3]_v + 1 — the quantum-dimension form of the spin coupling \tfrac12 \otimes \tfrac12 = 1 \oplus 0;

prop:frakD-energy-decomposition:

E \;=\; \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}(E + \sigma E)}_{\text{retained } (\cosh)}
\;+\; \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}(E - \sigma E)}_{\text{emitted } (\sinh)},

with the retained part bar-even (\sigma-fixed) and the emitted part bar-odd (\sigma-negated). The emitted (bar-odd, \sinh) channel is the bar-skew sector P_{\mathrm{skew}}; it vanishes iff E is purely retained.

thm:wedderburn-mass-formula:
Theorem Three-invariant atomic mass formula. Let (Z, N) be a neutral atom with atomic braid \mathcal{A} \in H_{A+Z}(q) (atomic braid). For each generator i of the braid, let M_i denote the 2 \times 2 transfer matrix obtained by chaining the crossing matrices of all strands j > i. Then the atomic mass is

  \mathfrak{m}(Z, N)
  =
  Z \cdot m_{\mathfrak{p}}
  + N \cdot m_{\mathfrak{n}}
  + Z \cdot m_e
  + \alpha\bigl(
      \Phi_1
      - 2[3]_q \cdot \Phi_2
      + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \cdot \Phi_3
    \bigr)

where:

  \Phi_1 = \sum_i \ln\bigl\lvert
    z \cdot (M_i)_{12} + (M_i)_{22}
  \bigr\rvert,
  \qquad
  \Phi_2 = \sum_i \ln\bigl\lvert
    \det M_i
  \bigr\rvert,
  \qquad
  \Phi_3 = \sum_i \ln\left\lvert
    \frac{\lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}}
         {\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}}
  \right\rvert.

The three invariants correspond to the three Wedderburn blocks of H_n(R, q):

Invariant Wedderburn block Matrix quantity
\Phi_1 standard (dim n{-}1) trace of Markov-weighted product
\Phi_2 sym \times alt determinant (product of eigenvalues)
\Phi_3 sym / alt ratio of eigenvalues (chirality)

The three invariants correspond to the three extremal Wedderburn blocks of H_n(R, q) (those associated with the symmetric [n], standard [n{-}1,1], and alternating [1^n] representations). These three extremal blocks exhaust the partition lattice if and only if n \le 3 (p(1)=1, p(2)=2, p(3)=3); already at n = 4 (p(4)=5), two non-extremal blocks [2,2] and [2,1,1] enter, and for A \ge 3 nucleons the adjacent-chain bridge count A - 1 grows strictly slower than the all-pairs count A(A-1)/2. The partition-by-partition computation (the formal derivation) computes all partitions exactly via Young's seminormal form in polynomial time. The mass functional uses the three extremal invariants as the leading-order formula; the full partition sum gives the exact Markov trace.

The coefficients are:

  • \alpha = m_e \times 8G (binding scale),
  • [3]_q = (q^3 - q^{-3})/(q - q^{-1}), the quantum 3-integer,
  • h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1}, the Hecke parameter, satisfying the exact algebraic dependency h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 = [3]_q - 3, i.e. 2\beta_3 + \beta_2 + 6 = 0 where \beta_2 = -2[3]_q and \beta_3 = h_{\mathrm{A}}^2.

prop:frobenius-s-classification:

Proof Proof of frobenius s classification. Each S-eigenvalue is checked in turn.

Coefficients. The action q \mapsto q^{-1} extends to the underlying field of fractions and acts on each coefficient:

  • D = q^4 + 4q^2 + 1 is palindromic in q^2: under q \to q^{-1}, D \to q^{-4} + 4q^{-2} + 1 = q^{-4}(1 + 4q^2 + q^4) = q^{-4} D. Then W_{\mathrm{sym}} = q^2/D \to q^{-2}/(q^{-4} D) = q^2/D, invariant. Same for W_{\mathrm{alt}}. For W_{\mathrm{std}}: (q^2+1)^2 \to (q^{-2}+1)^2 = q^{-4}(1+q^2)^2, so W_{\mathrm{std}} \to q^{-4}(1+q^2)^2 / (q^{-4} D) = W_{\mathrm{std}}.
  • [3]_q = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}: invariant under q \to q^{-1}.
  • h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} \to q^{-1} - q = -h_{\mathrm{A}}, so h_{\mathrm{A}} has eigenvalue -1 and h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 has eigenvalue +1.
  • z: at the canonical weight z = q^3/(q^2+1) the action gives z \mapsto 1/(q(q^2+1)) = z - h_{\mathrm{A}}, the negative-crossing loop value \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma^{-1}). So z is not an S-eigenvector: S exchanges the two loop values. Equivalently, the Markov trace commutes with S, \mathrm{tr}_M(S(X)) = S(\mathrm{tr}_M(X)), and the relation z(q^{-1}) = z(q) - h_{\mathrm{A}} is exactly the condition for this.
  • Catalan's constant G, Borromean volume 8G, electron mass m_e, and binding scale \alpha are real canonical constants unaffected by the algebraic action.

Functional \Phi_2. The transfer matrix is T(c, d) = \begin{pmatrix} ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d & c \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} with \det T = d(ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d) - c^2. The Frobenius antipode maps the primitive factor (c, d) to (\bar c, \bar d - \bar c h_{\mathrm{A}}), where the bar is q \mapsto q^{-1} on the coefficients (this swaps \sigma \leftrightarrow \sigma^{-1} and inverts q; without barring the coefficients, ud = (1, -h_{\mathrm{A}}/2) would map to (1, -3h_{\mathrm{A}}/2) rather than to itself). Direct computation:

See Table 3.

For each primitive the determinant is S-invariant. Since \det is multiplicative on chain products, \Phi_2 = \sum_i \log\lvert\det M_i\rvert is S-invariant.

Functional \Phi_3. Write an element of the two-strand Hecke algebra as X = c\,\sigma + d, with characters \chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(X) = cq + d and \chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(X) = -c q^{-1} + d (the eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of \sigma). The bar involution sends \sigma \mapsto \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h_{\mathrm{A}} and q \mapsto q^{-1}, so S(c\sigma + d) = \bar c\,\sigma + (\bar d - \bar c\,h_{\mathrm{A}}), where \bar{\ } is q \mapsto q^{-1} on the coefficients. It is a ring automorphism (semilinear over q \mapsto q^{-1}), so S of a chain product is the product of the barred factors.

Call X bar-homogeneous of sign \varepsilon \in \{\pm 1\} if \bar c = \varepsilon c and \bar d = -\varepsilon d. Two facts follow by direct expansion, using \bar h_{\mathrm{A}} = -h_{\mathrm{A}} and q - h_{\mathrm{A}} = q^{-1}:

  1. Character swap. If X is homogeneous of sign \varepsilon, then \chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(S X) = \varepsilon c\,(q - h_{\mathrm{A}}) - \varepsilon d = -\varepsilon\,\chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(X) and \chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(S X) = -\varepsilon c\,(q^{-1} + h_{\mathrm{A}}) - \varepsilon d = -\varepsilon\,\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(X).
  2. Closure. With \sigma^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}}\sigma + 1, (a\sigma + b)(c\sigma + d) = (ac\,h_{\mathrm{A}} + ad + bc)\,\sigma + (ac + bd). If the factors are homogeneous of signs \varepsilon, \varepsilon', every monomial of the \sigma-coefficient has bar-sign -\varepsilon\varepsilon' and every monomial of the constant term has bar-sign \varepsilon\varepsilon', so the product is homogeneous of sign -\varepsilon\varepsilon'.

The three primitives (1, 0), (1, -h_{\mathrm{A}}), (1, -h_{\mathrm{A}}/2) are homogeneous of sign +1 (the coefficient 1 is bar-invariant and 0, -h_{\mathrm{A}}, -h_{\mathrm{A}}/2 are bar-anti-invariant), and the unit (0, 1) is homogeneous of sign -1. By closure every chain product X_i entering \Phi_3 is homogeneous, of sign (-1)^{n-1} for n primitive factors, and by the character swap

  \frac{\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(S X_i)}{\chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(S X_i)}
  = \frac{-\varepsilon\,\chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(X_i)}{-\varepsilon\,\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(X_i)}
  = \left(\frac{\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(X_i)}{\chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(X_i)}\right)^{-1}.

The sign \varepsilon cancels, so only homogeneity matters, not the parity of n. The identity holds in the field of rational functions and so at every evaluation point where both characters are nonzero. Taking \log\lvert\cdot\rvert and summing over i gives \Phi_3(S(\beta)) = -\Phi_3(\beta), eigenvalue -1. (The argument holds over a generic field.)

Scope. The argument is for chains of bar-homogeneous factors, which includes every chain of the three primitives (and the nucleon and electron crossings of the same form). It is not a property of \Phi_3 on all of the Hecke algebra. For a general element, \chi^{\mathrm{sym}} and \chi^{\mathrm{alt}} are bar-equivariant, since both are ring homomorphisms and \chi(\sigma^{-1}) = \overline{\chi(\sigma)}. So S acts on \Phi_3, as on \Phi_1, by the evaluation flip q_0 \mapsto q_0^{-1}, which is not a sign change in general. Example: X = \sigma + 1 is not homogeneous, and the product of the two ratios is -(q+1)^2/(q-1)^2 \neq \pm 1, so \Phi_3 + \Phi_3 \circ S picks up 2\log\lvert (q_0+1)/(q_0-1) \rvert \neq 0 from this factor. Numerically, one finds \lvert\Phi_3 + \Phi_3 \circ S\rvert \lesssim 10^{-51} at the proton pin (mpmath, 50 digits) on all seven of its chains.

Functional \Phi_1. Because the canonical Markov trace commutes with S, S acts on \Phi_1 by inverting the evaluation point: \Phi_1(S(\beta); q_0) = \Phi_1(\beta; q_0^{-1}). The raw \Phi_1 is therefore not an S-eigenvector. It splits as \Phi_1 = \Phi_1^{+} + \Phi_1^{-} with \Phi_1^{\pm} = \tfrac12\bigl(\Phi_1(\beta) \pm \Phi_1(S(\beta))\bigr); the eigenvalue +1 in Table 1 is that of the projection \Phi_1^{+}, which is S-even by construction, and \Phi_1^{-} is S-odd. \square

Corollary. Since \Phi_2 is S-even and \Phi_3 is S-odd,

  \mathfrak{m}(S(\beta)) - \mathfrak{m}(\beta)
  = -2 \alpha \bigl(\Phi_1^{-}(\beta) + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3(\beta)\bigr).

The chirality term is the unique S-odd channel only when \Phi_1^{-} vanishes. It does not vanish in general: on the proton chain uud at the proton pin, \Phi_1^{-} \approx 0.0526 against h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3 \approx 0.00912, a ratio \approx 5.77.

Since S maps the proton braid (uud) to a braid with quark content (ddu), the S-odd part of the mass is the structural carrier of the proton-neutron splitting at the Wedderburn formula level, and it has two sources, \Phi_1^{-} and h_{\mathrm{A}}^2\Phi_3, not one.
cor:commutative-chirality-vanishes:
Corollary Chirality term vanishes in the commutative QOU limit. (From Frobenius S-classification applied in the commutative QOU limit.) In the commutative specialisation q \to 1, the chirality term h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3 in the Wedderburn mass formula (Wedderburn mass formula) vanishes identically:

  \lim_{q \to 1} h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \cdot \Phi_3 = 0.

Consequently the commutative atomic mass formula reduces to the two-term expression

where \alpha = m_e \cdot 8G and \lim_{q \to 1} [3]_q = 3.

prf:commutative-chirality-vanishes:
Proof Proof of commutative chirality vanishes. By Frobenius S-classification, h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} has S-eigenvalue -1, so h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 has eigenvalue +1. As q \to 1, h_{\mathrm{A}} \to 0 continuously, hence h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \to 0. The chirality functional \Phi_3 = \sum_i \log\lvert\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}_i / \chi^{\mathrm{alt}}_i\rvert remains finite (each per-factor ratio approaches \pm 1 classically; the sum of logs approaches 0 for any chain whose primitive factors include at least one ud crossing, and it approaches a finite limit otherwise). The product h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3 \to 0 \cdot \Phi_3 = 0.

For the quantum 3-integer: \lim_{q \to 1}[3]_q = \lim_{q \to 1}(q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}) = 3. \square

Companion reading. The crossing-energy interpretation of the commutative limit (commutative crossing energy) shows that the same vanishing h_{\mathrm{A}} \to 0 corresponds geometrically to the unit-circle parameterisation q = e^{i\varTheta}, where the crossing weight q - q^{-1} = 2i\sin\varTheta becomes pure imaginary. The two readings agree: the chirality channel collapses to zero in the strict commutative limit, while a unit-circle deformation recovers a non-trivial \mathrm{U}(1) phase.

rem:commutative-chirality-vanishes-inter: Remark Significance: chirality is the unique S-odd channel, trivial in the commutative limit. The chirality \Phi_3 — the unique S-odd channel by Frobenius S-classification — is therefore identically zero in the classical limit, and the mass formula degenerates to the two surviving S-even invariants \Phi_1 (trace) and \Phi_2 (determinant).

Let K_1, K_2 be two building block knots meeting at a crossing in a braid word \beta \in B_n. The transfer matrix of the crossing is:

where J_K(q) is the Jones polynomial of knot K and s = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2} is the Skein amplitude.

prf:wedderburn-mass-formula:
Proof Proof of wedderburn mass formula. Work over R = \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}] at generic q, passing to the fraction field where inverses are required; write h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} for the Hecke parameter and z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1) for the Markov weight, so that the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M is the linear functional normalised by \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1 and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_i) = z (positive stabilisation).

Step 1 — extremal Wedderburn blocks and channel eigenvalues. By the three-parameter decomposition, H_3(R, q) \cong M_1(R) \oplus M_2(R) \oplus M_1(R), with blocks labelled by the partitions (3), (2,1), (1,1,1); for general n the corresponding extremal blocks are the symmetric [n], standard [n-1, 1], and alternating [1^n] representations. The Hecke relation (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0 gives each generator the eigenvalue q in the symmetric channel and -q^{-1} in the alternating channel; since all \sigma_i are conjugate, the two one-dimensional blocks are the algebra characters \varepsilon^{\mathrm{sym}}(\sigma_i) = q and \varepsilon^{\mathrm{alt}}(\sigma_i) = -q^{-1}. A typed crossing element X = c \cdot \sigma_i + d \cdot \mathbf{1} (transfer matrix) therefore evaluates in the two scalar channels as

\lambda^{\mathrm{sym}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{sym}}(X) = cq + d,
\qquad
\lambda^{\mathrm{alt}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{alt}}(X)
  = -c q^{-1} + d .

Step 2 — the transfer matrix is the regular representation of the crossing algebra. A single crossing generates the two-dimensional commutative algebra R[\sigma] = R[x] / \bigl((x - q)(x + q^{-1})\bigr), in which \sigma^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}} \sigma + 1. In the ordered basis (\sigma, 1), multiplication by X = c\sigma + d has matrix exactly the crossing (transfer) matrix of the statement,

T(X) =
\begin{pmatrix}
  c h_{\mathrm{A}} + d & c \\
  c & d
\end{pmatrix},

since X \cdot \sigma = c\sigma^2 + d\sigma = (ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d)\,\sigma + c and X \cdot 1 = c\sigma + d. As a matrix of left multiplication, T is an algebra homomorphism: T(X)\,T(X') = T(XX'), which one verifies directly — XX' = c''\sigma + d'' with c'' = cc'h_{\mathrm{A}} + cd' + c'd and d'' = cc' + dd', matching the entries of the matrix product. Consequently, for the chained element X_i := \prod_{j > i} X_j of the crossings of all strands j > i, the transfer-matrix chain satisfies M_i = \prod_{j > i} T(X_j) = T(X_i), and reading off the basis coefficients gives (M_i)_{12} = (M_i)_{21} = c_i and (M_i)_{22} = d_i, where X_i = c_i \sigma + d_i. Moreover the eigenvalues of M_i = T(X_i) are precisely the two character values \lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{sym}}(X_i) and \lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}} = \varepsilon^{\mathrm{alt}}(X_i), since the regular representation of R[\sigma] diagonalises along its two characters. (Chaining within a single crossing algebra is the defining Level-0 transfer-matrix reduction; the exact all-partitions computation replaces it for n \ge 4, as the statement records.)

Step 3 — the three invariants are the three extremal block readouts.

  1. Markov trace (standard block). By linearity and the normalisation above, \mathrm{tr}_M(X_i) = c_i\,z + d_i = z\,(M_i)_{12} + (M_i)_{22}. Hence \Phi_1 = \sum_i \ln\bigl\lvert z\,(M_i)_{12} + (M_i)_{22}\bigr\rvert = \sum_i \ln\lvert \mathrm{tr}_M(X_i)\rvert is the Markov-weighted trace datum of the chain — the invariant attached to the standard (dim n{-}1) block in the correspondence table.
  2. Determinant = sym \times alt. Directly, \det T(X) = (ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d)\,d - c^2 = cdh_{\mathrm{A}} + d^2 - c^2 = (cq + d)(-cq^{-1} + d) = \lambda^{\mathrm{sym}}\lambda^{\mathrm{alt}}; equivalently this is the product of the two eigenvalues exhibited in Step 2. By multiplicativity of the determinant and of the characters, \det M_i = \lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\,\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}, so \Phi_2 = \sum_i \bigl(\ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\rvert + \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}\rvert\bigr).
  3. Ratio = sym / alt (chirality). \Phi_3 = \sum_i \bigl(\ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\rvert - \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}\rvert\bigr).

From 2 and 3, \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}}\rvert and \ln\lvert\lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}\rvert are recovered as half the sum and half the difference of the per-chain summands: the pair (\Phi_2, \Phi_3) is an invertible linear repackaging of the two one-dimensional block evaluations, while \Phi_1 carries the standard-block Markov datum. The triple (\Phi_1, \Phi_2, \Phi_3) therefore carries exactly the evaluations of the three extremal Wedderburn blocks on the chain — no more and no fewer. This is the claimed completeness at the 2 \times 2 transfer level: the chain data (c_i, d_i) \in R^2 of the two-dimensional crossing algebra support precisely the two characters and the Markov functional exhibited, and every block-respecting multiplicative invariant of \{M_i\} is a function of these three. For n \ge 4 the non-extremal partitions contribute additional invariants, computed exactly by the full partition sum via Young's seminormal form, as stated.

Step 4 — the coefficients. The overall scale \alpha = m_e \times 8G is the archimedean evaluation of the algebraic binding scale m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}_q(\mathcal{B}_3), with \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G the Borromean volume (binding scale). The determinant weight \beta_2 = -2[3]_q has a direct count: the three color channels give the pair count \binom{3}{2} = 3, q-deformed to [3]_q, with the sign fixed by the determinant sign accumulation and the factor 2 by the \mathfrak{p}\mathfrak{n} crossing-doubling convention established there. The chirality weight h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 is the minimal even power of the Hecke parameter compatible with the S-parity classification of the three terms (S-classification) and with the vanishing of the chirality contribution in the commutative limit (commutative chirality): h_{\mathrm{A}} \to 0 as q \to 1, so h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3 \to 0 and the classical mass formula retains no chirality term. All three weights are functions of q alone, evaluated at q_0, and the scale is fixed by m_e: no fitted parameter enters.

Assembling: the binding functional \alpha\,(\Phi_1 - 2[3]_q\,\Phi_2 + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2\,\Phi_3) is the weighted sum of the three extremal-block invariants of the atomic braid established in Steps 1–3, with the weights of Step 4, added to the free constituent masses Z \cdot m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N \cdot m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z \cdot m_e. \square

The numerical agreement of this formula with measured atomic masses across the nuclide table is an empirical cross-check, not part of the proof.
rem:level-zero-discards-braid-noncommuta:
Remark Level-0 discards braid non-commutativity at every n \geq 3, not only the non-extremal blocks at n \geq 4. The statement records that for n \geq 4 the Hecke algebra carries irreducible representations beyond the three extremal ones, and that the invariants they produce are not captured by the 2 \times 2 transfer matrix. That is a statement about the count of blocks. It is not a statement that the transfer-matrix construction is complete below n = 4, and reading it as one overstates the theorem.

A second approximation is present at every n \geq 3, independent of the block count. Step 2 of the proof forms the chained element X_i = \prod_{j > i} X_j inside the two-dimensional crossing algebra R[\sigma] = R[x] / \bigl((x - q)(x + q^{-1})\bigr), which is commutative, and sets M_i = T(X_i). The crossings so chained belong to different strand pairs, and the corresponding braid generators do not commute in H_n(q) for any n \geq 3. The Level-0 reduction therefore discards braid non-commutativity as well as the non-extremal blocks, and only the second of those is an n \geq 4 effect.

The two are easy to conflate because the dimensions agree at n = 3: the standard block of H_3(q) has dimension n - 1 = 2, and so does R[\sigma]. This is a coincidence of dimension, not an identification. By Step 2 the two eigenvalues of M_i are the symmetric and alternating characters \lambda_i^{\mathrm{sym}} and \lambda_i^{\mathrm{alt}}, so the standard representation does not act on M_i at all; the row labelled standard in the correspondence table records the Markov functional \mathrm{tr}_M(X_i) = z \, (M_i)_{12} + (M_i)_{22} on the crossing algebra, not an image of the two-dimensional block.

Deuterium is the unique atom with n = A + Z = 3. It is therefore both the smallest atom carrying two distinct braid generators and the only one at which the extremal blocks exhaust the partitions, which makes it the single point at which the two approximations can be separated. Evaluating the functional there gives

  \alpha\bigl(
    \Phi_1 - 2[3]_q \cdot \Phi_2 + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \cdot \Phi_3
  \bigr)
  \approx -6.214 \; \mathrm{MeV},

against a measured -B(\mathrm{D}) \approx -2.225 \; \mathrm{MeV}. Since no non-extremal block exists at n = 3, the discrepancy is attributable to the Level-0 reduction alone. It bounds the magnitude of that one approximation and excludes no ingredient of the construction. The evaluation, together with checks of the Step 2 readouts and of the commutativity of R[\sigma] against the non-commutativity of H_3(q), has been carried out exactly.
sec:mass-formula-derivation-commutative-:
Under the classical specialization q = 1, the Iwahori–Hecke algebra H_n(q) degenerates to the symmetric group algebra \mathbb{Q}[S_n], where the bar involution acts trivially and every braid word becomes indistinguishable from its mirror image. This section proves that the chirality pairing vanishes identically in the commutative limit q \to 1, demonstrating that non-zero mass splitting between chiral partners is a strictly quantum phenomenon proportional to h = q - q^{-1}.

Away from q = 1, Hoefsmit's explicit seminormal matrices equip each Wedderburn block V_\lambda with an orthogonal basis indexed by standard Young tableaux, on which the Jucys–Murphy elements act diagonally by content powers. Combining the Hoefsmit seminormal form with the figure-eight branching rule yields the derived mass formula for the light isotopes (A \le 4) directly from the per-partition character tables.

prop:hoefsmit-seminormal-form:
Proposition Hoefsmit seminormal matrices as R-matrix evaluations in H_n(q). For each partition \lambda \vdash n and aether parameter q > 1, the Hoefsmit seminormal form [hoefsmit1974] gives an explicit matrix representation \rho_\lambda\colon H_n(R, q) \to M_{d_\lambda}(\mathbb{C}) where d_\lambda = |\mathrm{SYT}(\lambda)| is the number of standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda. The generator \sigma_i acts on the basis of standard tableaux by:

  \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i)_{ss'}
  =
  \begin{cases}
    a_\rho & s' = s, \\
    b & s' = s_i, \\
    0 & \text{otherwise},
  \end{cases}

where s_i is the tableau obtained by swapping entries i and i+1 in s (if the result is a valid standard tableau), and the matrix entries are:

  a_\rho = \frac{q - q^{-1}}{1 - q^{-2\rho}},
  \qquad
  b = \sqrt{a_\rho \cdot a_{-\rho} + 1},

with \rho = c(s, i{+}1) - c(s, i) the axial distance (content difference) between the cells containing i{+}1 and i in tableau s.

These matrices satisfy the Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\,\sigma_i + 1 and the braid relation \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1}, and are the explicit R-matrix evaluations that dictate topological crossings in braid and knot diagrams.
